title: Lessons Learned from Historical Failures, Limitations and Successes of AI/ML in Healthcare and the Health Sciences. Enduring Problems, and the Role of Best Practices
venue: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Health Care and Medical Sciences, Health Informatics
extended_summary:
This book chapter reviews historical failures, limitations, and later successes in AI and machine learning, with an emphasis on lessons that can inform best practices for building and evaluating AI/ML systems in health care and the health sciences. Rather than reporting a new empirical study, it synthesizes case studies and methodological issues such as the Gartner hype cycle, AI winters, limitations of early neural networks and Bayesian learners, overfitting, model overconfidence, and mismatches between AI systems and real-world clinical needs.

The chapter is framed around the idea that many apparent AI breakthroughs were followed by setbacks, and that progress has often been non-monotonic. It discusses how later technical advances such as backpropagation, deep learning, support vector machines, random forests, Bayesian networks, and improved validation protocols addressed earlier shortcomings, while also noting that many of these methods still have important limitations, especially in low-sample or poorly designed settings.

The population and context are not an education sample; the material is entirely about health care and health sciences. The chapter argues for science-driven development, rigorous model selection and error estimation, appropriate data design, and cautious interpretation of benchmark and validation results. Its main conclusion is that many historical problems in AI/ML recur when methods are applied without proper theoretical grounding or alignment to real-world use cases, and that best practices are essential to avoid repeating past failures.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/book chapter-style review of historical AI/ML failures, limitations, and best practices in healthcare and the health sciences, not an empirical study. It does not evaluate an educational technology intervention or report a controlled design relevant to the requested topic.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct educational intervention effect is reported, and there are no student learning outcomes, comparators, or effect sizes. The chapter is not about ChatGPT-based support or middle school mathematics achievement/transfer.
